summary: Unexpected rate-tier shift and hourly metering bucket reassignment after batch migration
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden shift in how hourly usage was bucketed after a scheduled batch migration on 2026-03-09. Several hourly buckets for batch embedding jobs were reassigned to the subsequent hour, which caused a portion of usage to fall into a higher rate tier for that billing cycle.

Impact:
- BrightStore observed a ~12% increase in effective per-token cost for a two-hour window (01:00-03:00 UTC).
- Provisional overage alert triggered for their reserved-dedicated plan.
- Customer is requesting an explanation, provisional credit, and assurance this won't recur.

Environment:
- Org: BrightStore Inc. (dedicated pool: dp-us-east-07)
- Region: us-east primary; some jobs routed through eu-west for failover during the migration window.
- Job type: nightly batch embeddings (bulk-embed API, 16k sequence length), scheduled migration job id 'batch-mig-2026-03-09'

Steps to reproduce (from customer runbook):
1) Trigger the same batch job on prod during hourly rollover (01:58 UTC)
2) Observe metering events emitted by billing-pipeline at 02:00+
3) Compare hour buckets and rate tier assignment in the billing dashboard

Observed behavior:
- Metering pipeline shows a cluster of usage events stamped 01:59:xx that were routed into the 02:00 hourly bucket for aggregation and subsequently attracted higher tier pricing in the pipeline snapshot.
- Console shows a short-lived routing to eu-west for a subset of shards during the rollout.

Expected behavior:
- Usage should be aggregated into the hour corresponding to the request timestamp and rate-tier calculations should be stable across shard routing.

Attachments/Logs:
- Customer provided CSV of per-request timestamps and trace ids (attached in Jira).
- Linked billing snapshot and invoice preview in their account (screen grabs).
- Billing pipeline job logs: invoice-pipeline/consumer-20260309.log (internal link in investigation notes).

Requested outcome:
1) Clear explanation of why the hourly bucket reassignment happened.
2) Provisional credit for the delta while we investigate.
3) Fix or mitigation to prevent reoccurrence and confirmation of re-rating if credit is applied.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - BrightStore (customer): We ran our nightly embed at 01:58 UTC and saw a spike in invoice preview. Support requested help — attaching CSV of timestamps and trace ids.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Support (Maya Patel): Thank you. I've triaged this and opened a P1 ticket. We've applied a temporary billing hold on new overage notifications while we investigate. Assigning to SRE/Platform to look at metering pipeline behavior (assigned to Liam).

2026-03-10 11:30 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Initial look at invoice-pipeline logs: there were several rebalances in the batch scheduler between 01:58 and 02:02 UTC. Not yet sure if event timestamps were mutated by the rebalance. Pulling audit trail for consumer offsets and shard routing.
2026-03-10 14:02 - Finance (Elena Ruiz): Please note BrightStore has requested a provisional credit. Finance requests an initial delta estimate to approve temporary credit up to $6,000.
2026-03-11 08:47 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer confirmed they are okay with provisional credit while root cause is investigated. Waiting on SRE findings and precise usage delta calculation.

2026-03-12 16:20 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Found related consumer-offset race in consumer-v2; committing investigation notes to linked PR. Suspect timestamp normalization failed to account for shard-handback during rebalance. Preparing backfill plan.
investigation_notes: Query: SELECT count(*) FROM metering.events WHERE org='brightstore' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-03-09T01:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-09T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY hour_bucket; result shows 24% of events with request_ts in 01:59 but hour_bucket=02:00.
Observed short-lived routing to eu-west for shards 12-14 at 01:59:55 UTC documented in cluster logs: scheduler_events/2026-03-09/rebalances.log#L342-L358.

Hypothesis A: consumer-v2 rebalance path re-emitted events without applying timestamp normalization, causing aggregator to compute hour_bucket from processing_time instead of request_time for a subset of events.

Hypothesis B: a recent change in invoice-pipeline (PR #889) adjusted buffer flush logic and altered offset boundaries for hour aggregation. Investigating PR diff and test coverage for hour boundary cases.

Evidence: consumer-v2 log lines show 'processed_ts' differing from 'request_ts' by 5-8 seconds for affected traces; aggregator currently uses 'max(processed_ts, request_ts)' in the presence of missing fields, which may bias toward processed_ts during rebalance.
Dashboard links: billing-dashboard.redwood/internal/org/brightstore/usage?window=2026-03-09T00:00:00Z..2026-03-09T04:00:00Z; metering-latency panels show spikes exactly at 02:00 UTC.
Temporary mitigation applied: billing hold for BrightStore to stop automated overage emails and prevent auto-charge while we compute a corrected rerate.
Next step: run re-aggregation backfill for 2026-03-09 01:00-03:00 and compute delta with current invoice preview. Backfill plan in progress; estimating 2 hours to run and validate.
resolution_summary: Partial mitigation: provisional billing hold applied and provisional credit approved by Finance up to $6,000 pending exact delta. Backfill job scheduled to recompute hour buckets for 2026-03-09 01:00-03:00. Final rerating and any additional credits will be applied after backfill completes.
root_cause: Under investigation — preliminary evidence points to a consumer-v2 rebalance re-emitting events where aggregation used processed_ts instead of request_ts for hour bucketing; change in invoice-pipeline buffer flush (PR #889) may have widened the window for the race.
follow_up_actions: Run re-aggregation backfill for 2026-03-09 01:00-03:00 and produce corrected invoice delta (owner: Liam, ETA: 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC).
If backfill confirms delta > provisional credit, submit for additional finance approval and apply credits to BrightStore billing account (owner: Elena).
Add unit/integration test for hour boundary in invoice-pipeline and increase test coverage for consumer rebalance scenarios (owner: backend team).
Create post-incident runbook entry describing rebalance→bucketing risk and mitigation (owner: Platform Ops).
Schedule follow-up call with BrightStore to review findings and confirm credit application (owner: CS).
